title: Ancient Greece
intro: Gods, heroes, theatres and the very first Olympic Games.

questions.prompt: Where were the ancient Olympic Games held?
questions.explanation: The ancient Olympic Games were held at Olympia, in southern Greece, in honour of the god Zeus.

questions.prompt: Which Greek city-state was famous for its strong army and tough training?
questions.explanation: Sparta trained its boys to be soldiers from a young age and was known for its powerful army.

questions.prompt: Which ancient Greek city is known as the birthplace of democracy?
questions.explanation: In Athens, citizens could vote on decisions. This early form of democracy is still remembered today.

questions.prompt: In Greek myths, who was the king of the gods?
questions.explanation: Zeus ruled the gods from Mount Olympus and was the god of the sky and thunder.

questions.prompt: The ancient Greeks watched plays in open-air theatres.
questions.explanation: Greek theatres were built outdoors, often into hillsides, so large crowds could see and hear the actors.

questions.prompt: In the Greek myth, how did the Greeks get soldiers inside the city of Troy?

options.label: They hid inside a wooden horse

questions.explanation: The story says Greek soldiers hid inside a giant wooden horse, which the people of Troy pulled into their city.

questions.prompt: Which famous temple stands on the Acropolis in Athens?
questions.explanation: The Parthenon was built on the Acropolis hill as a temple to the goddess Athena.

questions.prompt: Athena was the Greek goddess of what?
questions.explanation: Athena was the goddess of wisdom and was also linked to war and crafts. Athens was named after her.

questions.prompt: The ancient Olympic Games were held every four years.
questions.explanation: The games took place every four years, a tradition the modern Olympics still follow.
